trial_court: Chief Judicial Magistrate, Salem, H.M.O.P. No. 171 of 1986
facts_of_case: Wife married husband in 1977, had a daughter, and lived together until 1984 when misunderstandings arose. Wife left husband's house and filed M.C. No. 9 of 1985 for maintenance, which was granted by the trial court at Rs. 250/- per mensem from 31.3.1986 onwards.

legal_principles.principle: A Hindu wife is entitled to be maintained by her husband during her lifetime.
legal_principles.held: Section 18(1) of the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, which came into operation on 21.12 1956, a Hindu wife, whether married before or after the commencement of that Act, shall be entitled to be maintained by her husband during her lifetime.
applicable_acts_sections: Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act — Section 18

legal_principles.principle: The right to claim maintenance or litigation expenses under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act is a special statutory right.
legal_principles.held: It is thus clear that the right to claim maintenance or litigation expeneses under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, is not made available generally to the parties to a marriage, but only when a proceeding between the spouses is pending under that Act, and in that respect, the right conferred under Section 24 of that Act, is in the nature of a special statutory right not in any manner outside the provisions Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act.

outcome.final_order: Respondent should pay petitioner maintenance at the rate of Rs. 250/- per mensem from 31.3.1986 onwards, having regard to the income of the respondent.

use_for_drafting: advising on Hindu Marriage Act provisions
